title: 1 Enoch
by: Translated by David Robert Palmer (2026); from chapter 40 mostly Richard Laurence (1883), as edited by Palmer
note: Palmer gives priority to the Greek where it survives; chapters 1–32 are his own translation of the Greek and chapters 1–39 are newly translated. From chapter 40 the text is mostly Richard Laurence’s, which Palmer is revising, and in the last chapters it follows Laurence’s numbering. His notes are given after each chapter.
credit: David Robert Palmer, The Book of Enoch the Prophet (2026 update), dedicated to the public domain.

b.p: 1The word of the blessing of Enoch, how he blessed the righteous elect, who will be living in the time of trouble; when all those who oppose, that is, the wicked and the ungodly, are to be removed, and the righteous be saved.
2And Enoch took up his parable, and said, "Enoch, a righteous man, who walked with God, answered and said, that his eyes were opened, to see a holy vision that was in the heavens from God.

He showed me, and I heard, holy words of the holy ones, and as I heard everything from them I also understood what I saw. And I speak not for this generation, but for generations which are far ahead at a distant period, on account of the elect.
Upon their account I spoke and conversed with Him.
3 He will go forth from his dwelling, the Holy and Mighty One, the God of the cosmos.
4The Eternal God will appear out of the highest heaven with tremendous power, and set foot upon Mount Sinai. He will emerge from among the troops of his mighty power.
5Everyone will be smitten with fear, and the Watchers tremble.

6Great fear and terror will seize them all, to the ends of the earth. The lofty mountains will shake and collapse and crumble, the high hills melt down like wax in the face of a flame. The earth will split open with a chasm, and all things which are in it perish; while judgment shall come upon all, even upon all the righteous.
7But with them he shall make peace, they shall receive shouts of blessing. He shall preserve the elect, and toward them exercise clemency.
8Then shall all belong to God; be happy and blessed; and the splendor of the Godhead shall illuminate them.

9Behold, he comes with ten thousands of his holy ones, to execute judgment upon all, and to destroy the wicked, and to convict all flesh of all their works of ungodliness which they have ungodly commtted, and of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.1

notes: 1:9 Quoted in the Epistle of Jude, verses 14, 15.

b.p: 1Observe all the works in the heaven, how they have not altered their ways, and the luminaries which are in the heaven, how they all rise and set, each one marshalled forward in its proper order in time, and their seasons showing forth, and not deviating from their own assignment.
2Look at the earth, and contemplate the operations that take place in it from beginning to completion, how they do not change, not one of them upon the earth, but all appear to you the works of God.
3Behold summer and winter, that the earth is replete with water; and that the clouds, the dew, and the rain, alight upon it.
1Consider and behold the trees, how they appear to wither, and every leaf falls off, except for fourteen trees,
whose leaves do not fall off, but the old ones remain until the new ones come after two or three years.

1And again consider the days of summer, how the sun begins to be an enemy above.2 You look for shelter and shade because of the heat of the sun, and the ground is burning with scorching heat, and you cannot step either on the dirt or on the rock because of its heat;

notes: 4:1 Or, "begins to be directly opposite above."

b.p: 1how the trees are sheltered with green leaves, and all their fruits result in value and glory. Contemplate and realize regarding all these works of His, and understand that the Living God has made them so, even He who lives in all the ages.

2And His works, all that he has ever done from year to year, are all happening this way; that is, all his works whatsoever, finish for Him, and their operations do not deviate, but just as He has ordered, all the works come to pass.
3Behold how the sea and the rivers likewise carry out His word and do not deviate their operations from it.

4You, however, have not persevered, nor performed according to his instructions, but have turned away. And you complain against His Majesty in proud and harsh words with your unclean mouths. You hard-hearted. Because you complain with your false accusations, there is no peace for you.
5So you will curse your days, since you will ruin the years of your life. And your damnation will be multiplied by everlasting cursing, and there will be no mercy or peace for you.

6At that time your names will be as eternal curses to all the righteous, and they will all call down curses, with you as the curse; and all the sinners and the ungodly will also swear using you. And all the humble servants will rejoice, and there will be for them a ransoming of sins, and a release of all compassion and peace and reasonableness. There will be for them a healing, pleasant light. And they will inherit the earth. And all you sinners, you will experience no healing, but rather a putting down upon you all, cursing.
7The things coming to the elect are light, joy and peace, and they will inherit the earth. But for you, the ungodly, there will be a curse.

8At that time light and joy will be given to the elect, and they will inherit the earth. Then, wisdom will be given to all the elect, and they will all live, and no longer sin, neither against the truth, nor according to pride. And there will be light shone in a person, and a knowing, wise, perception, and they will never err.

9Neither will they sin all the days of their lives, and they will certainly not die by the fury of wrath, but will complete the number of their days, and their lives will thrive in peace, and the years of their rejoicing will be multiplied with exultation and eternal peace all the days of their lives.
1And3 it came to pass that when the humans multiplied, daughters were born in those days, attractive and beautiful.
2And the Watchers,4 sons of heaven, saw them, and desired them, and said to one another, "Come, let us choose wives for ourselves from the humans, and beget our own children."
3And Semyaza, who was their leader, said to them, "I am afraid, that you do not really intend to carry out this plan, and I will be liable for a great sin all alone."
4So they answered him, "Let us all swear an oath, and bind one another with a curse, not to turn back from our intention until we have carried out this plan and completed it."
5They all then swore an oath, and bound each other with a curse.
6Now they were two hundred who had descended in the days of Jared5 to the top of Mount Hermon.6 And they named the mountain Hermon, because on it, they had sworn and bound each other with a curse.7
7And these are the names of their captains: Semyaza, (he was the leader over all), Aratak, Kimbra, Sammaney,
Daniel, Arearosh, Semiel, Yomiel, Khokhariel, Yezekiel, Batriel, Satiel, Atriel, Tamiel, Barakiel, Anantna, Toniel, Hramiel, Azael, Hrakiel, Touriel.<sup class="fn" data-fn="8">8</sup>
8These are their captains over ten.

notes: 6:1 The first two extracts made by Syncellus from the Greek start here, and end with the 15th verse of chap. 10.

6:2 The Greek text says "angels," here, and an Aramaic text says "Watchers" (J.T. Milik, Aramaic Fragments of Qumran Cave [Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1976], p. 167). The original text was certainly not written in Greek, but in Hebrew or Aramaic.
6:6a The name Jared in Hebrew means "descent," so there is a play on words in the original Hebrew.

6:6b Greek: Ἑρμονιειμ, which imitates the Hebrew plural, so some might render this "the peaks of Hermon." Yet it was an idiom in Hebrew to pluralize that which was high, awesome, mysterious, great. But what could be properly plural is "curses."
6:6c Hermon in Hebrew means "consecrated." Charles (p. 63) says Mt. Hermon derives its name from the Hebrew word herem, a curse.

6:7 See the table of the differing names made by R. H. Charles at the end of this document. The Aramaic texts preserve an earlier list of names of these Watchers: Semihazah; Artqoph; Ramtel; Kokabel; Ramel; Danieal; Zeqiel; Baraqel; Asael; Hermoni; Matarel; Ananel; Stawel; Samsiel; Sahriel; Tummiel; Turiel; Yomiel; Yhaddiel (Milik, p. 151).

b.p: 1And they, and all the rest with them, took wives for themselves; they selected a woman for themselves, one each. And they proceeded to go in to them and be defiled with them. And they taught them sorceries and incantations, and demonstrated herbal potions to them.

2And the wives got pregnant, and gave birth to three races. First, the huge giants, three thousand cubits tall.9 The giants brought forth10 the Naphelim, and the Naphelim brought forth the Elioud. And they were increasing in power in accordance with their size.
3They ate up the crops of the humans, and thus the humans were not able to supply enough food for them.
5Then the giants turned against humankind, to devour them.
6And they began to violate the birds, and beasts, and reptiles, and fish, and began to eat the flesh of one another, and were drinking the blood.
7Then the earth joined in after the manner of those lawless ones.

notes: 7:2a Using the smallest known cubit, this would be 4,375 feet tall, or 1,332 meters.

7:2b Jubilees says "slew." Jubilees 7:21-22 "‘ The Watchers took unto themselves wives...and they begat sons the Nâphîdîm...and they devoured one another, and the Giants slew the Nâphîl and the Nâphîl slew the Eljô and the Eljô mankind." The Ethiopic does not mention the three classes of giants, but one Greek text does, and Charles says that 3 classes of giants are presupposed by 86:4 and 88:2, and that the archetype must have had them.

b.p: 1Azael taught humans to make swords and daggers and shields and breastplates, the teaching of angels, and showed them metals and the working of them, and bracelets and ornaments and antimony and eye make-up, and all sorts of choice stones, and dyes.11
2And godlessness became prevalent, and they were committing sexual sins, and were led astray and became corrupted12 in all their ways.
3Semyaza taught incantations and root cuttings; Amarosh the release of spells; Barakiel astronomy; Kokiel portents; Satiel astrology; Zariel the ways of the moon.13
4Then, as humankind was being annihilated, a cry went up to heaven.

notes: 8:1 One Greek text adds here: καὶ ἐποίησαν ἑαυτοῖς οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ ταῖς θυγατράσιν αὐτῶν, καὶ παρέβησαν καὶ ἐπλάνησαν τοὺς ἁγίους.
8:2 Greek: ἀφανίζω, became hidden, unseen. Became unrecognizable, because so transformed for the worse, like fruit rots and changes its appearance completely.

8:3 Black follows a longer text and reads "Semhazah taught spell-binding and the cutting of roots; Hermoni taught the loosing of spells, magic, sorcery and sophistry. Baraqel taught the auguries of the lightning; Kokabiel taught the auguries of the stars; Zikiel taught the auguries of fire-balls; Arteqif taught the auguries of earth; Simsel taught the auguries of the sun; Sahrel taught the auguries of the moon. And they all began to reveal secrets to their wives."

b.p: 1So at that time, Michael and Uriel and Raphael and Gabriel, these looked down from heaven, and saw the great quantity of blood being spilled upon the earth.
2And they said to one another, "The sound of their cries upon the earth has reached the gate of heaven.
3"The souls of humans are pleading, saying, 'Take our case in before the Most High.' "

4And they said to the Lord, "You are the Lord of lords, and the God of gods, and the King of the Ages. The throne of your glory lasts into all the generations of the world, and your name will be holy and great and praised into all the ages.14
5For you have created all things, and have all authority over them, and everything is transparent and uncovered before you.

6And you see all that Azael has done, who introduced every sort of wickedness upon the earth, and has disclosed the eternal mysteries that are in heaven, which humans pursue and have now come to know;
7and also Semyaza, to whom you have given authority to be chief over them simultaneously with him.
8And they have gone to the daughters of the mortals of the earth, and slept with them and polluted them, and revealed to them all kinds of sins.
9And the women have given birth to giants, because of whom the whole earth is filled with blood and wickedness.
10And now, behold, the souls of those who have died are crying out, and pleading as far as the gate of heaven. And the groans of the remnant ascend, that they are not able to
escape from the face of the wickedness taking place on the earth.
11And you know all things before they happen, and you see these things, and yet you are tolerating them, and not telling us anything must be done about these things."15

notes: 9:4 See Luke 1:49-50, where Mary says "And holy will be his name, and his mercy to those who fear him, into age after age." One Greek text adds here, surely mistakenly and out of sequence, τότε ὁ ὕψιστος ἐκέλευσε τοῖς ἁγίοις ἀρχαγγέλοις, καὶ ἔδησαν τοὺς ἐξάρχους αὐτῶν καὶ ἔβαλον αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον, ἕως τῆς κρίσεως. "Then the Most High urged on the holy arch-angels, and they bound their leader and cast him into the abyss, until the judgment."
9:11 One Greek text indicates that Gabriel was the one speaking on behalf of the four.

b.p: 1Then the Most High spoke, the Great and Holy One. And speaking to Uriel, he sent him to Noah the son of Lamech, saying as follows,

2"Tell him in my name: 'Hide yourself.' And reveal to him the end that is coming near, how the whole earth is perishing, that a deluge is about to take place over the entire earth, and will destroy everything that is in it.
3And instruct him how he will escape, and his seed will abide into all generations for ever."
4And to Rafael he said, "Bind Azael hand and foot, and cast him into darkness; that is, split open the desert which is in Dudael, and throw him in;
5and place him under rocks jagged and sharp, and cover him over in darkness, and there he must dwell for the age. Yes put a lid over his face, and he will not see light.
6And on the day of the great judgment he will be led off to the blazing fire.

7And heal the earth, which those angels have corrupted, and proclaim life to the earth, so that they may heal the plague, and not all the sons of humankind perish by all the mysteries which the Watchers told them and taught their children.
8And since the whole earth has been devastated, corrupted through the works of the teachings of Azael, ascribe to him the whole offense."

9And to Gabriel the Lord said, "Go out against the illegitimate children, the mutants, the offspring of the fornication, and erase those children of the Watchers out of humankind. Send them into a war of mutual destruction.16 For length of days shall not be theirs.
10And there will be all kinds of entreaties for them by their fathers, and also for themselves, because they hope to live eternal life, and to live each one of them 500 years."
11And to Michael He said, "Go out and inform Semyaza and the rest with him who are merging with the women to be contaminated with them in their uncleanness,

12that when their offspring devour each other and they see the destruction of their loved ones, then you shall bind them for seventy generations in the chasms of the earth, until the days of their judgment and the time of the end, until the final judgment as been passed for all eternity.
13At that time they shall be led off to the fiery abyss. In torture and in prison they shall be locked up for all eternity.
14And whoever shall be burned and destroyed from now on, they will be chained up together with them until the end of all generations.
15I shall destroy all the spirits of the bastard offspring of the Watchers, since they have damaged humankind.17
16And destroy every oppressor from the face of the earth, and make every work of iniquity vanish. And then will
appear the plant of righteousness and truth for evermore. With joy shall it be planted.
17And now all the righteous will escape, and will live until they beget a thousand generations, and all the days of their youth and of their old age they will complete in peace.
18At that time the whole earth will be cultivated with righteousness, and wholly planted with trees, and overflowing with blessings.

19And every plant of the earth that is planted will rejoice. And a vine will be planted, and from the vine that is planted they will make a thousand jugs of wine, and of all the seed that is sown each measure will bear a thousand, and every seah of olives produce ten baths of oil.
20And you, cleanse the earth of every uncleanness and from every unrighteousness and from every sin and unglodliness. And of every impurity that has risen upon the earth, wipe it clean.
21And all the people will be working for me, and blessing me and worshiping me.
22And the earth will be cleansed of every pollution and every uncleanness and base impulse. And punishment I will not again send upon it, for all generations for ever.

notes: 10:9 Jubilees 5, "And he sent among them his sword that each one should kill his neighbor; and they commenced to kill each other, till they all fell by the sword, and were destroyed from the earth. But their fathers looked on, and after that were bound in the abysses of the earth till the day of the great judgment."
10:15 Here end the first two extracts made by Syncellus.

b.p: 1And at that time I will open the store-rooms of blessing that are in heaven, to bring them down upon the labors, upon the products of the children of humankind.
2And in those days, truth and peace will commune with them as one, for all the days of eternity, for all the generations of humankind."
1Before these things, Enoch was concealed; and none of the people knew where he was concealed, where he had been, or what had happened to him.
2And his activities had to do with the Watchers, and his days were with the holy ones.
3And I, Enoch, was standing blessing the Lord of majesty, the King of the Ages, and behold, the Watchers of the great and holy one called to me, Enoch the scribe,18

4and they19 said to me, "Enoch, scribe of righteousness, go and say to the Watchers of heaven who have deserted the lofty sky and their holy everlasting station, who have been polluted with women, and have done as the sons of men do and taken wives for themselves, and become completely corrupt on the earth,
5that there shall never be peace or remission of sin for them. And as for their offspring, in whom they have joy,
6they will watch the slaughter of their beloved. And over the doom of their children they will lament and petition without end, and there will be no mercy or peace for them."

notes: 12:3 Laurence's translation says the Watchers called him Enoch the Scribe, as a sort of parenthetical note. The others indicate that Enoch called himself this. Regardless, in v. 4 the Watchers call him "Enoch, scribe of righteousness."

12:4 Laurence's translation of the Ethiopic has God being the one addressing Enoch, whereas all the other translations have the Watchers telling Enoch to go tell the Watchers something. The question arises, was it all the watchers who fell, or only a portion of them? If only a portion then we could have here the watchers who remained holy telling Enoch to go talk to the fallen watchers. In chapter 1 there are still Watchers watching in the end times when Christ returns to earth, so I conclude that not all the Watchers fell.

b.p: 1So Enoch said to Azael, "Be gone. There will be no peace for you. A severe sentence has been issued against you, to fetter you,
2and you shall have neither relief nor appeal, because of all the works of ungodliness and the harm and sin which you have demonstrated to humans."
3Then I went and spoke to all of them, and they were all afraid, and terror and trembling seized them.
4And they asked me in any way possible to write for them petitions asking that their children be forgiven, and that I make certain their petitions are remembered before the Lord of heaven,
5because they themselves could no longer speak to, nor lift their eyes toward, heaven, for the shame of how they had sinned, and were condemned.
6Then I wrote down their reminders and petitions, and their supplications regarding their spirits and regarding being fettered, if somehow there might be forgiveness, or delay.
And I went off, and sat down at the waters of Dan in the
7 land of Dan southwest of Hermon, reading out their petitions and supplications; thus I fell asleep.
8And behold, dreams came to me, and a vision fell upon me, and I saw a vision of wrath and punishment. And a voice came, saying, "Speak this to the sons of heaven, to reprimand them."
9And when I awoke I went to them, and they were all gathered together, sitting and weeping, with their faces covered, in Abel-maim, which is between Lebanon and Senir.
10I recounted before them all the visions I had seen while asleep, and proceeded to speak the words of justice to them, reprimanding the Watchers of heaven.
1A record of the words of justice and reprimand of the Watchers from eternity, as ordered by the Great and Holy One in the aforementioned vision.
2"I saw in my sleep what I will now speak with a tongue of flesh, with the breath of my mouth (which the Great One has given to humans with which to speak) and with the understanding of my heart,
3which also was put forth sealed, and issued to reprimand the Watchers of the offspring of heaven.
4I had written down your entreaties for the angels, and in my vision the following was revealed: That your entreaties were not even received;
5that from now on you will never ascend into heaven for all the ages, and it is ordered that you be fettered in the prisons of the earth for all the generations of the world,
6and that regarding your beloved children, you will watch their destruction, and you will be of no help to them, but they will fall by the sword before your eyes.
7and your entreaties concerning them will not stand, neither the ones about yourselves, and you, weeping and pleading and sincerely speaking everything from the document I have written.
8And this is how the vision appeared me. Behold, clouds were summoning me, and a mist was calling to me, and the paths of the stars and lightning bolts began to guide and
urge me on, and the winds in my vision conducted me in flight,
9and raised me up and carried me into heaven. And I advanced until I reached a wall built of hailstones that had tongues of fire swirling around them. And it was beginning to scare me.

10And I went into the tongues of fire, and approached a large house made of hailstones, and the walls of the house were like a mosaic of hailstones, all of crystalline snow, and its floor was of crystalline snow.
11And the upper areas were like the paths of stars and lightning bolts, and in the midst of them were fiery cherubim, and their ceiling was water.
12And fire was flaming around its walls, and its doors burned with fire.
13When I entered into that house, it was hot like fire and cold like ice, and nothing conducive to life was in it. Fear enveloped me, and trembling took hold of me.
14And as I was shaking and trembling, I fell down. In my vision, I was looking,
15and behold, another door was open before me, and this house was bigger than the other, and entirely constructed of tongues of fire,
16and in every respect excelling in spendor and awesomeness and magnificence, such that I am unable to describe to you all its splendor and magnificence.
17Its floor was fire, while its upper areas were like lightning bolts and paths of stars, and its ceiling was flaming fire.
18So I was surveying it, and I saw a high throne, and its appearance was like crystalline ice, and its circumference
like the shining sun, and there were sightings<sup class="fn" data-fn="20">20</sup> of cherubim.
19And out from under the throne were flowing rivers of flaming fire, and it was impossible to gaze upon them.
20And great was the glory of the one sitting on the throne. His raiment was like seeing the sun, but brighter, and whiter than any snow.
21And no angel coming into this house could see his face, by reason of its splendor and glory; and no flesh was able to look upon him.
22A blazing fire encircled him, and a great fire stood before him, and no one would come near him. Myriads of myriads stood before him in a circle, and his every word was a deed.
23And the holy angels who were near him do not turn away from him either by night or by day, nor to they depart from him.
24And till this point I was prostrate on my face, and trembling. Then the Lord called to me with his mouth and said to me, "Come here, Enoch, and listen to my word."
25And one of the holy ones came to me and spoke to me and made me stand, and he led me up to the entrance. But I lowered my face and bent down.

notes: 14:18 The Greek says ὄρος "mountain," which Charles says is a corruption of ὅρασις, sighting. The translations of the other languages say sound or voice of cherubim.

b.p: 1And He spoke up and said to me: 'Do not be afraid, Enoch, you true human being, and scribe of truth and righteousness. Come here and listen to my voice.' And I heard his voice.
2'Go to the Watchers of heaven, those who sent you to petition for them, and say to them, "You are supposed to petition for humans, and not humans for you.

3By what rationale do you forsake the lofty and holy heaven, which endures for ever, and sleep with women, and become unclean with the daughters of humans, and take for yourselves wives just as the children of earth do, and beget children for yourselves, even giants as sons?

4You were holy, and spirits that live for ever, yet you became unclean with the blood of women, and begat children with the blood of flesh, and with the daughters of humans. And you lusted after flesh and blood just as they do who die and perish.
5For this reason I have given them females: so they might put seed in them and in this manner produce children with them, so that none of the work on the earth will vanish.
6But you were spirits that live for ever, and not dying throughout all the generations of eternity.
7This is why with you I did not create females; you were spirits of heaven, your dwelling-place was in heaven.
8And now the giants, who were produced from spirits and flesh, will be spirits mighty upon the earth, and on the earth shall their dwelling-place be.

9Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; for since they came into existence from higher beings, and holy Watchers were the source of their creation and first foundation, they will be called evil spirits.
10The spirits of heaven, their dwelling-place will be in heaven, and the spirits which they have produced on the earth, their dwelling-place will be on the earth.
11And the spirits of the giants are a malevolent cloud, corrupt and fallen, and working against and overthrowing
the earth; hard and giant spirits, and making haste and eating nothing, but are spirits hungry and thirsty and always attacking.
12And these will rise up against the children of humankind and women, because they came from them in the days of slaughter and destruction and death.

1The Nephalim, the spirits which came forth from their bodies, will go on destroying, uncondemned. Thus they will destroy until the day of the end, until the great judgment, in which the great aeon will be completed.
2And now about the Watchers, who are sending you to petition for them, who used to be in heaven:

3'You were in heaven, and there was no mystery that was not revealed to you— even the mystery of God you have come to know; and in the hardness of your hearts this you disclosed to the women, and by this mystery the females and humankind have multiplied wickedness over the earth.'
4Say therefore to them: 'There will be no peace for you.' "
1And they took me, and carried me away, to where the beings were like blazing fire, and whenever they wanted, would appear as humans.
2And they carried me to a gloomy place and to a mountain, whose summit reaches to heaven.
3And I saw the place for the luminaries, and the storehouses of the stars and of the thunders, and I saw into
the airy pathways, where there was a bow of fire and its arrows and their quivers and all the lightning bolts.
4And they carried me to waters and to a fire in the west, which is also the receiver of every setting of the sun.
5And we came to a river of fire in which the fire flows down like water, and pours into the great ocean toward the west.
6I saw all the big rivers, and I reached the great river, and arrived at the great darkness, and went where [no] flesh walks.
7And I saw the mountains of the darkness of winter and the place where all the waters of the deep pour out.
8I saw the mouth of all the rivers of the earth and the mouth of the deep.
1I saw the storehouses of all the winds. I saw how He arranged all the supports and the foundation of the earth with them, and I saw the corner stone of the earth.
2I saw the four winds which support the earth
3and the firmament of heaven.
4I saw the winds of heaven which turn and direct the course of the sun, and all the stars.
5I saw the winds over the earth which carry the clouds. I saw the extremities21 of the earth, with the supports of the heaven upon them.
6I proceeded on, and saw a place which burns night and day, where there were seven mountains of precious stones, three toward the east and three lying toward the south.
7And the ones toward the east, one was of colorful stone, one was of pearl, and the other of antimony; those toward the south were carnelians.
8But the middle one which reached up to heaven as the throne of God, was of alabaster,22 and the top of the throne was of sapphire.
9And I saw a blazing fire. Beyond these mountains
10there is a place on the other side of the great extent of the earth; there the heavens come to an end.
11And I saw a deep chasm, with pillars of fire descending, and they were not measurable either in depth or in height.

12And beyond this yawning chasm I saw a place which had no firmament of heaven above it, nor foundation of earth beneath it, nor was there water in it or birds, but it was a desolate and fearsome place.
13I saw there seven stars as great burning mountains, about which when I inquired,
14an angel said to me, 'Until the consummation of heaven and earth, this is the prison for the stars and the powers of heaven.

15And the stars which are rolling over in the fire, these are those who transgressed the command of the Lord at the beginning of their rising— because their place coming out of the heaven is empty— because they did not come out at their proper time.
16And He was angered by them, and He has bound them until the time of the completion of the punishment for their sins, for ten thousand years.

notes: Isaiah 40:22- “He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its people are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a canopy, and spreads them out like a tent to live in.” Genesis 1:6,7 “And God said, ‘Let there be an expanse between the waters to separate water from water. So God made the expanse and separated the water under the expanse from the water above it. And it was so.” Gen 1:17- “God set the [the sun and moon] in the expanse to give light on the earth.” That says the sun and moon are this side of the upper waters, and local and close. It is the same place God said he placed the birds, v. 20. The upper waters did not all fall during the flood. The Psalmist in Psalm 148:4 still much later in time said: “Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and ye waters that be above the heavens.” Psalm 19 says the sun moves above the earth, “In them (the firmament of the heavens) he has set a tabernacle for the sun, which is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoicing as a strong man to run his course. His going forth is from the end of the sky, and his circuit unto the ends of it; and there is nothing hidden from its heat.” Job 38:14 says, “The earth takes shape like clay under a seal.” And that shape is flat, and circular, with upturned edges. I could go on, but you can see that the Book of Enoch is in harmony with the Bible as to the shape of the earth.

18:8 Greek: φουκα, which Charles, p. 49, footnote 15, says is a transliteration of ךְוּפּ the Aramaic form of, that is, stibium/antimony. "Alabaster" is the reading of Laurence, Charles, and Schodde; Knibb says "stibium" and Black says "emeralds."

b.p: 1And Uriel said to me, "The angels who copulated with women, and whose spirits assumed many different forms and contaminated humankind and led them astray to sacrifice to demons, this is where they will stay until the great judgment, in which they will be distinguished for final condemnation.
2And their women, those who took the side of23 the angels, they will become sirens."24
3And I, Enoch, I alone saw these visions, the endings of all things, and no other human may see as I have seen.

notes: 19:2a Greek: παραβαίνω- go by the side of, aor part act masc/neut gen pl

19:2b Greek: σειρῆνας - "sirens." Both Charles and Black say that this Greek word הנעי σειρήν in the LXX usually renders the Hebrew - "desert owl," but also sometimes "jackal," both of which were known for their plaintive cry. See Mic 1:8; Jer 27:39(50); Is 13:21; Job 30:29; Is 34:13; 43:20. The desert owl is also reputed to be beautiful and attractive in appearance. I have rendered the Greek text as best I could: καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες αὐτῶν τῶν παραβάντων ἀγγέλων εἰς σειρῆνας γενήσονται. Below are the other translations. I find the first three preposterous, as if the women were responsible for the angels falling. However, what IS the moral duty of people who are over-powered and captured by evil ones? They still must not "take the side of" the evil ones. If they do, there is some punishment. Not fair to the poor women, some might cry. If they did not take the side of the angels, they would have been killed. Yes, and the men also, if forced by the fallen ones to do things they did not consider right and they refused, they would also be killed, and no doubt many men were killed. Women must realize that the average man is still in danger of being overpowered by a stronger man or crazier man, and certainly could be overpowered by fallen angels. But here, God knew the hearts of the women, and judged accordingly. Regardless, they could have refused and been killed, and received an eternal blessing instead of judgment. Laur.: their wives...who led astray the angels of heaven that they might salute them. Schod: their women having led astray the angels of heaven, will be like their friends Knibb: their wives, having led astray the Angels of Heaven, will become peaceful. Charles: the women of the angels who went astray shall become sirens. Black: the wives of the angels who transgressed shall become sirens.

b.p: 1These are the angels of power:
2Uriel, one of the holy angels, he is over the world and over Tartarus.
3Raphael, one of the holy angels, he is over the spirits of human beings.
4Raguel, one of the holy angels, he judges the service of the luminaries.
5Michael, one of the holy angels, he is over the good people assembled for battle and over the genuine.
6Sariel, one of the holy angels, he is over the spirits whose sinning is in the spirit.
7Gabriel, one of the holy angels, he is over Paradise and over the serpents25 and over the cherubim.
8Remiel, one of the holy angels, he is whom God set over those who rise. These seven are called arch-angels.

notes: 20:7 Greek: δρακόντων which can also mean dragons. Laurence's translation hints at Sheol, or the dwelling-place of dragons. Sheol/Hades was divided into dwelling-places for the righteous dead (Paradise) and the unrighteous, so this could possibly be referring to the Hades/hell for the unrighteous. Black proposes in parentheses "seraphim."

b.p: 1And I proceeded until I came to a formless void.
2And in that place I saw a terrifying work: I observed neither a heaven above nor did I see ground holding anything up, but a chaotic and terrifying place.
3And I saw seven stars of heaven who had been bound and cast in there, which were like great mountains that were burning with fire.
4Then I said, "For what charge were they bound, and why were they cast here?"

5Then Uriel said to me (he was one of the holy angels who was with me, and who was chief over them), he said to me, "Enoch, about whom are you asking, and about whom are you so eager to find out the truth?
6These are the stars of heaven who transgressed the command of the Lord, and He bound them here for ten thousand ages, until the due time for their sins is completed."
7And from there I passed on to another place, this even more terrifying, and I saw fearsome operations. Much fire

was there burning and flaming, and it had a chasm that reaches as far as the abyss, with many huge columns of fire going down. I could not make out either its length or its width, nor could I even guess.
8Then I said, "How terrifying this place is, and how painful to look at!"

9Then Uriel responded to me, one of the holy angels who was with me, and he said to me, "Enoch, why are you this afraid and terrified?" And I answered, "Because of this dreadful place and the sight of such pain."
10And he said, "This place is a prison for the angels. Here they will be imprisoned for an eternity."
1From there I proceeded to another spot, where he showed me in the west a great and high mountain, of hard rock, and having four hollow places in it.

2They were deep, and wide, and very bare. Three of them were dark, and one of them was lit and had a spring of water in the middle of it. And I said, "How bare these caverns are, and such deepness and darkness a sight to behold!"

3Then Raphael, one of the holy angels, who was with me, responded and said to me, "These hollow places exist to gather together the spirits, that is, the souls of the dead. In them they are sorted apart. Here, all the souls of human beings are collected.
4And in these places their confinement is appointed, until the days of their judgment, and until the distinction and dividing of the time at which that great judgment will be upon them."
5I observed a dead man who was pleading, and his cry was advancing as far as heaven, and pleading there.
6And I inquired of Raphael, the angel who was with me, and said to him, "This spirit pleading, whose is it, whose cry advances so, and pleads until it reaches heaven?"

7And he answered me saying, "This is the spirit which came from Abel, whom Cain the brother murdered. And Abel will plead concerning him, until his seed perishes from the face of the earth, until his seed vanishes from the seed of humankind."
8Then I asked about all the enclosing of the pits, by which one was separated from the other.

9And he answered me, saying, "Those three departments were made to separate the spirits of the dead, and the spirits of the righteous are separated by a chasm into this one, which has a spring of water, and light in it.26
10And then this one was made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth and judgment has not happened to them during their lifetime.27

11Here their spirits are separated for this horrible torment, until that great day of judgment, of punishment, and the torment of being cursed for ever. This was the due repayment for their spirits. He will bind them there for ever.
12And then this division was made for the spirits of those who have complaints, who have disclosures concerning their destruction, when they were slaughtered in the days of sinners.

13And this department was made for the spirits of those people who were not purely pious but sinning, and would fellowship with the lawless. They were not completely lawless, but with the lawless they collaborated. Those enduring here will receive a lesser punishment than the lawless; their spirits will not be punished in the day of judgment, yet neither will they be raised from here."
14Then I blessed the Lord of glory, and said, "Blessed are you, righteous Lord, who rules for all time."

notes: 22:9 See the gospel of Luke 16:26 where the righteous dead are separated from the unrighteous dead by a chasm.
22:10 cf. 1 Corinthians 11:31 "For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged." Many people spend their whole lives keeping safe from accountability and judgment.

b.p: 1And from there, I went to another place toward the west, toward the extremities of the earth.
2And I observed a fire running along without ceasing or deviating from its course either by day or by night, but it ran continually.
3And I inquired, saying, "What is this, which never ceases?"
4Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me,
5"This stream of fire toward the west is the fire which tends all the luminaries of heaven."
1And from there I went to another place on the earth and he showed me a mountain of fire that blazed day and night.

2And I went beyond it and saw seven magnificent mountains all differing each from the other, and adorned with rocks magnificent and beautiful, valuable and precious, glorious in their shapes. Three mountains were toward the east, one founded on the other, and three
toward the south, one upon the other, and with deep rough ravines, no one of which joined with any other.
3And the seventh mountain was in the middle of these,28 surpassing them in height, was like the seat of a throne, and fragrant trees surrounded it.

4And among these was a tree such as I had never smelt before, and none of the others smelled like it, nor does any other. It had a sweet fragrance more aromatic than all others, and its leaves and its blossoms and its branches never wither. And as for its fruit, it was similar to the cluster of the date palm.
5Then I said, "How beautiful this tree is, and how fragrant, and how lush the leaves, and its blossom delightful to the eye!"
6At that time Michael, one of the holy angels who was with me— and he was leading them—

notes: 24:3 Schodde p. 107: "Having mentioned that the tree of life is to be transplanted to the New Jerusalem, he now visits that place. As the Greeks thought Delphi, the centre of their worship, the middle of the earth, the Jewish seer here regards Jerusalem as such, as it is possibly already done, Ezek. 38:12 v. 5; Isa. 2:2, and book of the Jubilees, 7:2, where Zion is called the navel of the earth, like the term ὀμφαλός, used of the round stone in the temple at Delphi as the centre of the earth in Pindar P. 4, 131; 6,3."

b.p: 1he then said to me, 'Enoch, why are you asking about and why are you marveling at the fragrance of the tree, and why do you want to find out its truth?'
2Then I answered him, 'I want to know about everything, but very much about this tree especially.'
3And he answered saying, 'This highest mountain, the summit of which is like the throne of God, is the seat where
the great and holy Lord of glory, the King of the Ages, sits, when he comes down to visit the earth with blessing.

4And as for this fragrant tree then, no flesh has the right to partake of it until the great judgment, in which there will be the recompense of everyone, and a consummation for ever. Then those who are righteous and pure will be given that right.
5The fruit of it is for the elect unto life. On the sides of the north, even in a holy place will it be transplanted,29 near the temple of God, the King of the Ages.30

6At that time they will be exceedingly glad and rejoice and go into the holy place; its fragrances will be in their bones, and they will live a long life on the earth as your fathers lived; and also, in their days no sufferings or blows or punishments will happen to them.'
7Then I blessed the God of glory, the King of the Ages who prepared such things for the righteous, and created them and promised to give such to them.

notes: 25:5a "transplanted," Greek- μεταφυτευθήσεται. The Tree of Life was originally located in the Paradise of Adam (Genesis 2:9), but is now transplanted to this holy place near the temple of God. See note on Enoch 32:3 below.

25:5b See LXX Psalm 47:2-3 Μέγας κύριος καὶ αἰνετὸς σφόδρα ἐν πόλει τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν, ὄρει ἁγίῳ αὐτοῦ, 3 εὖ ῥιζῶν ἀγαλλιάματι πάσης τῆς γῆς. ὄρη Σιων, τὰ πλευρὰ τοῦ βορρᾶ, ἡ πόλις τοῦ βασιλέως τοῦ μεγάλου, And Psalm 24:3-5 "Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place? He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart; who hath not lifted up his soul unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully. He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation."

b.p: 1And from there I proceeded to the middle of the earth, and I saw a blessed place, in which there were trees, saplings surviving and sprouting from a tree that was cut off.
2And there I observed a holy mountain; underneath the mountain water from the east, and it had two branches flowing toward the south.
3And I saw toward the east another mountain higher than that one, and between them a deep ravine, not wide, and near it water proceeded underneath the mountain.

4and toward the west of it another mountain lower than that one and not very high, and a deep and sterile ravine between them, and another deep and sterile ravine and dry land at the far end of the three mountains.
5And all these deep ravines were of hard rock, and no tree was taking root in them.
6And I marvelled about the ravines, and was very much amazed.
1And I said, "What is the meaning of this blessed land full of trees but then this accursed chasm?"

2Then one of the holy angels31 who was with me answered and said, 'This accursed chasm is for those who are accursed, until the end of the age. Here will be collected all those who are accursed, who say inappropriate things with their mouths against the Lord, and speak hard things about his glory. Here they will be collected, and here will be their dwelling-place.
3In the final ages, in the days of the righteous judgment in front of the righteous, at each their time, the ungodly will bless the Lord of glory, the King of the Ages.
4In those days of their judgment, they will bless for mercy, insofar as he distributes it to them.'
5Then I blessed the Lord of glory, and I magnified and sang of his glory, as is appropriate.

notes: 27:2 The Greek text does not say which angel is speaking. Knibb has Raphael, and the rest of the translations say Uriel.

b.p: 1And from there I proceeded to the middle of a mountain in the wilderness, and I saw it deserted and solitary,
2full of trees from the seeds, and a river of water, not from rain coming down from above,
3conducting abundant water toward the north-west, and from all quarters there went up spray and mist.
1Still farther from there I went to another place in the wilderness, heading east from that mountain,
2and I saw trees of judgment, aromatic of frankincense and myrrh, and their fruit trees were similar to almond trees.
1And beyond these, I went not much farther to the east, and saw another place, with canyons of water,
2in which was a beautiful tree, aromatic like the mastic tree,
3and along the rims of these canyons I perceived aromatic cinnamon; and beyond these I headed toward the east.
1And I saw some other mountains, and on them groves of trees that had a resin coming out of them, called styrax and galbanum.
2And beyond these mountains I saw another mountain toward the east with slopes of dirt, and they all alike were replete with trees in the likeness of almonds,
3which when rubbed, are better smelling than all other fragrances.
1After these fragrances, in the north toward the east I saw seven mountains full of choice nard, and fragrant trees, and cinnamon, and pepper.

2And from there I passed on to the start of all those mountains, far toward the east of the earth, and I passed above the Erythraean Sea, and its farthest point, and from this I passed above Zotiel.32

3And I arrived at the Garden of Innocence, and saw at a distance from those trees, more trees,33 with large, beautiful branches, attractive and magnificent, and also the tree of knowledge, whose fruit they eat and know great wisdom.
4This tree was as tall as the fir tree, but its leaves like the carob tree, and its fruit like a very beautiful cluster of grapes, and its smell spreads a long way from the tree.
5At that time I said, "How beautiful this tree is, and how pleasing its appearance!"

6Then Raphael, the holy angel who was with me, answered, "This is the tree of knowledge, from which your forefather ate, and your ancient mother, which when they ate they learned of knowledge, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven from the garden."

notes: 32:2 Zotiel- The Greek text has only Ζωτιηλ, and the Ethiopic adds "the angel." Matthew Black's translation here reads "the (great) darkness." In his commentary, Black, p. 179, says "the (great) darkness See note on 17.6. Milik, 234, L. 21, seeks to explain the extraordinary variant of G Eth. 'over the angel Zotiel' as having arisen by corruption of ζόφος (or ζοφώδης); cf. 17.2 εἰς ζοφώδνη τόπον. Eth. mal'ak "angel" could have arisen through its similarity to mal'elto = ἐπάνω αὐτῆς. Dillmann took the reading as genuine and suggested that the angel Zotiel was defending the entrance to Paradise. The name is otherwise unknown, unless we identify it with Sithwa'el, the angel of 'winter' and therefore the 'dark regions' (cf above at 6.7). A corruption of the text seems more probable." In The Origin of the Names of Angels and Demons in the Extra-Canonical Apocalyptic Literature to 100 A.D. by George A. Barton ( https://www.jstor.org/stable/3260228) the name Zotiel is said to mean "the little one of God;" yet the only appearance given thereof is this verse in the Ethiopic, and he is only speculating about its Aramaic derivation. In the Dictionary of Angels by Gustav Davidson, p. 330, Zotiel is listed as one of the "princes of paradise." But again, on what basis? Only this here?

32:3 The Greek text has καὶ μεγάλα δύο μὲν ἐκεῖ, which we may assume would be both the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. The Greek also has οὗ ἐσθίουσιν ἅγιοι τοῦ καρποῦ αὐτοῦ, "the fruit of which the holy ones eat." Whereas Charles' translation does not include the tree of life, but does include the word "holy," except he attaches the nominative-case ἅγιοι as an adjective modifying fruit, καρποῦ, and reads "holy fruit." ?! So one has to decide which story line you are going with: the one which has the tree of life, or the one without the tree of life. The translations of Laurence, Schodde, Knibb and Black do not have the word holy, and also do not then have the tree of life, which are consistent, unlike that of Charles. Combine this with another alleged problem: In this part of Enoch, the Garden is in the east, in accord with the Old Testament in the Bible, see Genesis 2:8,9 (which also indicates that the Tree of Life was there). But in Enoch 77:3 the Garden of Innocence is in the north. Milik thinks that the author wished "to unify the two traditional locations," and consequently, he recognizes one Paradise of righteousness only, located in the northwest. Black (p. 179) states "It is impossible, however, to reconcile these two conflicting traditions. They are, no doubt, an inevitable consequence of 'conflation' of two traditions, the oriental locating paradise in the east and the hellenistic which places Elysium in the west." The question remains whether this document should follow the Greek text which includes the two trees found in Gen. 2:8,9 or go with having only the tree of knowledge, as found in all four of the consulted translations. Charles, p. 72, says "If δύο μέν is right, then τὸ δένδρον τῆς ζωῆς should be inserted before καὶ τὸ δένδρον τῆς φρονήσεως. But the evidence of xxiv-xxv is decidedly against this; for according to xxiv. 2-xxv the tree of life is in the neighborhood of the chief of the seven great mountains. Now these mountains are in the NW. but the earthly Paradise is in the NE. xxxii.1; lxxvii. 3. The passages from the Zohar quoted by Laurence and subsequenly adduced by Lods and Lawlor in support of δύο μέν as the true reading do not necessarily support their contention." He goes on to point out that those passages refer to the Slav. Enoch, and the first of them to the Paradise which is a part of Sheol/Hades, not this Paradise; and another passage in Slav. Enoch still does locate Paradise in the neighborhood of the chief of the seven great mountains. I say why could it not be that the "paradise of Adam" is distinct from the paradise in heavenly Zion, to where the Tree of Life in the Greek is said to have been "transplanted"? (Enoch 25:5 - μεταφυτευθήσεται) These are visions by Enoch. There is no reason he could not have been shown both a vision of the Tree of Life in the holy mount Zion, and also the Tree of Life in the paradise of Adam. In heavenly visions Enoch need not be restricted by time. Why could Enoch not see a vision of two different eras, and the Tree of Life therefore being in two locations because of the difference in time?

b.p: 1From there I went on toward the extremities of the earth; where I saw large animals each different from the other, and birds various in their form, beauty, and call.

2To the east of these animals I perceived the extremities of the earth, whereon the heavens come to rest. The gates of heaven stood open, and I saw how the stars of the heaven come forth. I counted the gates out of which they proceeded, and wrote them all down, as they came out one by one according to their gate of exit. I wrote down their names according to their constellations, their times and their seasons, as the angel Uriel, who was with me, pointed them out to me.
3He showed me everything, and wrote it down.
4He also wrote down for me their names, their regulations, and their operations.
1From there I went on toward the far northern parts of the earth.

2And there I saw a great and glorious wonder at the farthest parts of the whole earth. I saw there heavenly gates opening into heaven. The northern winds proceed from them. When they blow, there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew, and rain.
3And from one of the gates they blow for blessing; but when they blow from the other two gates, it is with violence and harm. They blow over the earth violently.
1From there I went to the extremities of the world westwards; and I saw there, as I had seen in the north, three open gates and as many outlets.
1And from there I proceeded to the extremities of the earth southwards; where I saw three gates open, from which issued mist, rain, and wind.

2From there I went to the extremities of heaven eastwards; where I saw three heavenly gates open toward the east, which had smaller gates above34 them. Through each of these small gates the stars of heaven pass, and run their course toward the west by a path which is shown to them.
3And when I beheld them, I blessed; and I will continually bless the Lord of glory, who has wrought these

great and glorious wonders so that they might display the magnificence of his works to his angels and to the spirits and to the souls of humankind, so they in turn might all praise his works and operations; so all his creatures might see the effect of his power; so they might glorify the great work of his hands; and bless him for ever.
1The second vision which he saw, a vision of wisdom, which Enoch saw, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan, the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam.

2The following is the commencement of the word of wisdom, which I received to declare and to tell to those who dwell on the earth. "Hear, you people of ancient times, and understand, you ones in future times, the words of the Holy One, which I will utter in the presence of the Lord of spirits.
3To those who were before, it would have been good to mention it, but from those in future times we shall not withhold the sum of wisdom.

4Until now there has not been imparted to anyone from the Lord of spirits such wisdom as I have received, because of my capacity of understanding, and according to the good pleasure of the Lord of spirits, from whom I have received the inheritance of eternal life.
5These three parables then, were imparted to me, and I lifted up my voice, and I declared them to those who inhabit the earth.
1The first parable: When the congregation of the righteous shall be manifested, and sinners are judged for their sins, and are driven from the face of the earth.

2When the Righteous One shall be manifested in the presence of the righteous and elect, whose works depend upon the Lord of spirits, and when the light shall appear to the righteous and elect who dwell on the earth, where then will the habitation of sinners be? And where will the resting-place be, for those who have rejected the name of the Lord of spirits? It would have been better for them if they had not been born.35
3When the secrets of the sinners shall be revealed unto the Righteous One, then shall they be judged; and the godless ones shall be driven from the presence of the righteous and elect.

4From that time on, those who now possess the earth shall not be powerful, nor exalted. They shall not be able to look upon the countenances of the holy; for the light of the Lord of spirits will have appeared on the faces of the holy, the righteous, and the chosen.
5Then shall the mighty kings be destroyed when they are given over into the hands of the righteous and the holy.
6And from that time on none of them shall plead for mercy before the Lord of spirits, because for them life will be at an end.
1And it will come to pass in those days that the elect and holy children will come down from the high heaven and their offspring will become one with the children of humans.36
2Enoch received books of indignation and wrath, books causing panic and agitation:
2"Never shall they obtain mercy," says the Lord of spirits.
3At that time a cloud snatched me up, and a whirlwind raised me above the face of the earth, and it set me down at the extremity of the heaven.

4There I saw another vision. I saw the habitations and resting places of the saints. There my eyes beheld their habitations with the angels, and their resting places with the holy ones. And they were entreating, supplicating, and interceding on behalf of the children of humans. And righteousness flowed out before them like water, and mercy like dew was scattered over the earth. And thus shall it be with them for ever and ever.
5At that time my eyes beheld the dwelling of the Elect One, who is True, Faithful, and Righteous.
6And countless shall be the number of the holy and the elect in his presence for ever and ever.

7I saw how they dwell under the wings of the Lord of spirits. And all the holy and elect were singing before him, and they shone like the brightness of fire; their mouths being full of blessings, and their lips praising the name of the Lord of spirits. And righteousness shall never cease before him, and truth never fail in front of him.

8I was desirous of remaining there, and my soul longed for that abode. For there my lot had previously fallen, and my inheritance was already assigned; for thus it had been resolved about me37 before the Lord of spirits.
9At that time I glorified and extolled the name of the Lord of spirits with blessing and with praise; for he has strengthened me for blessing and praise, according to the will of the Lord of spirits.
10For a long time did my eyes contemplate that place. I blessed him, and said, Blessed be he, blessed from the beginning until eternity.
11In his presence there is no end; he knows before the world was created what the world is and would be, even during generation after generation.’
12Those not sleeping bless you, and they stand before your glory, and bless and praise and exalt, saying, “Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of spirits; he fills the earth with spirits.”
13And there, my eyes saw all those awake, standing in front of him, and blessing and saying, “Blessed are you, and blessed is the name of the Lord, for ever and ever!
14Then my countenance38 changed, such that I could no longer look.

notes: 39:1 This verse is quite unclear. The expression “the elect and holy” usually refers to members of the righteous human congregation, but in the Ethiopic it seems to be referring to angels, who will come down, resemble the form of humans, and oppose humanity again. Another interpretation is that the tenses in verses 1 and 2 were originally past tense, and here is a retelling of the fall of the watchers, and that they bred with humans, and the Lord gave Enoch books of indignation and wrath. It would read thus: <sup>1</sup> It came to pass that the elect and holy sons of the highest heaven descended, and their seed became mingled with the children of humans. <sup>2</sup> Enoch received books of indignation and wrath, books causing panic and agitation: <sup>2</sup> "Never shall they obtain mercy," said the Lord of spirits. <sup>3</sup> Now a cloud snatched me up, and a whirlwind raised me above the face of the earth, and set me down at the extremity of the heaven.”
39:8 So Charles, Schodde, Knibb and Black; Laurence: “for thus I had prevailed before the Lord of spirits.”
39:14 That is, his mood for state of mind changed.

b.p: 1After this I beheld thousands of thousands, and myriads of myriads, and an infinite number of people, standing before the Lord of spirits.

2On the four wings likewise of the Lord of spirits, on the four sides, I perceived others, besides those who were standing before him. Their names, too, I know; because the angel, who proceeded with me, declared them to me, discovering to me every secret thing.
3Then I heard the voices of those upon the four sides magnifying the Lord of glory.
4The first voice blessed the Lord of spirits for ever and for ever.
5The second voice I heard blessing the Elect One, and the elect who suffer39 on account of the Lord of spirits.
6The third voice I heard petitioning and praying for those who dwell upon earth, and supplicate the name of the Lord of spirits.
7The fourth voice I heard expelling the impious angels,40 and prohibiting them from entering into the presence of the Lord of spirits, to prefer accusations against41 the inhabitants of the earth.
8After this I besought the angel of peace, who proceeded with me, to explain all that was concealed. I said to him,
Who are those whom I have seen on the four sides, and whose words I have heard and written down? He replied, The first is the merciful, the patient, the holy Michael.

9The second is he who presides over every suffering and every affliction42 of the sons of men, the holy Raphael. The third, who presides over all that is powerful, is Gabriel. And the fourth, who presides over repentance, and the hope of those who will inherit eternal life, is Phanuel. These are the four angels of the most high God, and their four voices, which at that time I heard.

notes: ["Impious angels." Literally, "the Satans" (Laurence, p. 45; Knibb, p. 128). Ha-satan in Hebrew ("the adversary") was originally the title of an office, not the name of an angel.]

b.p: 1After this I beheld the secrets of the heavens and of paradise,43 according to its divisions; and of human action,44 as they weigh it there in balances. I saw the mansions of the elect, and the abodes of the holy.45 And there my eyes beheld all the sinners, who denied the Lord of glory, and whom they were expelling from there, and dragging away, as they stood there; no punishment proceeding against them from the Lord of spirits.

2There, too, my eyes beheld the secrets of the lightning and the thunder; and the secrets of the winds, how they are distributed as they blow over the earth: the secrets of the winds, of the dew, and of the clouds. There I perceived the place from which they issued forth, and became saturated with the dust of the earth.

3There I saw the wooden46 receptacles out of which the winds became separated, the receptacle of hail, the receptacle of snow, the receptacle of the clouds, and the cloud itself, which continued over the earth before the creation of the world.

4I beheld also the receptacles of the moon, whence the moons47 came, whither they proceeded, their glorious return, and how one became more splendid than another. I marked their rich progress, their unchangeable progress, their disunited and undiminished progress; their48observance of a mutual fidelity by a stable oath; their proceeding forth before the sun, and their adherence to the path allottedthem,49 in obedience to the command of the Lord of spirits. Potent is his name for ever and for ever.

5After this I perceived, that the path both concealed and manifest of the moon, as well as the progress of its path, was there completed by day and by night; while each, one with another, looked toward the Lord of spirits, magnifying and praising without cessation, since praise to them is rest; for in the splendid sun there is a frequent conversion to blessing and to malediction.

6The course of the moon’s path to the righteous is light, but to sinners it is darkness; in the name of the Lord of spirits, who created a division between light and darkness, and, separating the spirits of men, strengthened the spirits of the righteous in the name of his own righteousness.
7Nor does the angel prevent this, neither is he endowed with the power of preventing it; for the Judge beholds them all, and judges them all in his own presence.

notes: by an oath to which they adhered.
to their path. [Or, "the sun goes out first and completes its journey" (Knibb, p. 129; cp. Charles, p. 122).]

b.p: 1Wisdom found not a place on earth where she could inhabit; her dwelling therefore is in heaven.

2Wisdom went forth to dwell among the sons of men, but she obtained not a habitation. Wisdom returned to her place, and seated herself in the midst of the angels. But iniquity went forth after her return, who unwillingly found a habitation, andresided among them, as rain in the desert, and as a dew in a thirsty land.

1I beheld another splendor, and the stars of heaven. I observed that he called them all by their respective names, and that they heard. In a righteous balance I saw that he weighed out with their light the amplitude of their places, and the day of their appearance,50 and their conversion. Splendor produced splendor; and their conversion was into the number of the angels, and of the faithful.
Then I inquired of the angel, who proceeded with me,

2 and explained to me secret things, What their names were. He answered. A similitude of those has the Lord of spirits shown you. They are names of the righteous who dwell upon earth, and who believe in the name of the Lord of spirits for ever and for ever.
1Another thing also I saw respecting splendor; that it rises out of the stars, and becomes splendor; being incapable of forsaking them.
1Parable the second, respecting these who deny51 the name of the habitation of the holy ones, and of the Lord of spirits.

2Heaven they shall not ascend, nor shall they come on the earth. This shall be the portion of sinners, who deny the name of the Lord of spirits, and who are thus reserved for the day of punishment and of affliction.

3In that day shall the Elect One sit upon a throne of glory; and shall choose their conditions and countless habitations, while their spirits within them shall be strengthened, when they behold my Elect One, for those who have fled for protection to my holy and glorious name.
In that day I will cause my Elect One to dwell in the
4 midst of them; will change the face of heaven; will bless it, and illuminate it for ever.

5I will also change the face ofthe earth, will bless it; and cause those whom I have elected to dwell upon it. But those who have committed sin and iniquity shall not inhabit it,52 for I have marked their proceedings.53 My righteous ones will I satisfy with peace, placing them before me; but the
condemnation of sinners shall draw near, that I may destroy them from the face of the earth.

notes: In the Bodleian MS. there seems here an evident omission. This omission is supplied in the Paris MS. I have followed the latter.

b.p: 1There I beheld the Ancient of days,54 whose head was like white wool, and with him another, whose countenance resembled that of man. His countenance was full of grace, like that of one of the holy angels. Then I inquired of one of the angels,55 who went with me, and who showed me every secret thing, concerning this Son of man; who he was; whence he was and why he accompanied the Ancient of days.

2He answered and said to me, This is the Son of man, to whom righteousness belongs; with whom righteousness has dwelt; and who will reveal all the treasures of that which is concealed: for the Lord of spirits has chosen him; and his portion has surpassed56 all before the Lord of spirits in everlasting uprightness.

3This Son of man, whom you behold, shall raise up kings and the mighty from their dwelling places, and the powerful from their thrones; shall loosen the bridles of the powerful, and break in pieces the teeth of sinners.

4He shall hurl kings from their thrones and their dominions; because they will not exalt and praise him, nor humble themselves before him, by whom57 their kingdoms were granted to them. The countenance likewise of the mighty shall He cast down, filling them with confusion.
Darkness shall be their habitation, and worms shall be their bed; nor from that their bed shall they hope to be again raised, because they exalted not the name of the Lord of spirits.

5They shall condemn the stars of heaven, shall lift up their hands against the Most High, shall tread upon and inhabit the earth, exhibiting all their acts of iniquity, even their works of iniquity. Their strength shall be in their riches, and their faith in the gods whom they have formed with their own hands. They shall deny the name of the Lord of spirits, and shall expel him from the temples, in which they assemble;
6And with him the faithful,58 who suffer in the name of the Lord of spirits.

notes: The Chief or Head of days, Dan. vii. 9.
The words, Then I inquired of one of the angels, are omitted in the Bodleian MS. They occur in the Paris MS.
["Shall expel him…the faithful." Or, "will be driven from the houses of his congregation, and of the faithful" (Knibb, p. 132; cp. Charles, p. 131).]

b.p: 1In that day the prayer of the holy and the righteous, and the blood of the righteous, shall ascend from the earth into the presence of the Lord of spirits.

2In that day shall the holy ones assemble, who dwell above the heavens, and with united voice petition, supplicate, praise, laud, and bless the name of the Lord of spirits, on account of the blood of the righteous which has been shed; that the prayer of the righteous may not be intermitted before the Lord of spirits; that for them he would execute judgment; and that his patience may not endure for ever.59

3At that time I beheld the Ancient of days, while he sat upon the throne of his glory, while the book of the living was opened in his presence, and whileall the powers which were above the heavens stood around and before him.

4Then were the hearts of the saints full of joy, because the consummation60 of righteousness was arrived, the supplication of the saints heard, and the blood of the righteous appreciated by the Lord of spirits.

notes: [That his patience…endure for ever." Or, "(that) their patience may not have to last for ever" (Knibb, p. 133).]

b.p: 1In that place I beheld a fountain of righteousness, which never failed, encircled by many springs of wisdom. Of these all the thirsty drank, and were filled with wisdom, having their habitation with the righteous, the elect, and the holy.
2In that hour was this Son of man invoked before the Lord of spirits, and his name in the presence of the Ancient of days.

3Before the sun and the signs were created, before the stars of heaven were formed, his name was invoked in the presence of the Lord of spirits. A support shall he be for the righteous and the holy to lean upon, without falling; and he shall be the light of nations.

4He shall be the hope of those whose hearts are troubled. All, who dwell on earth, shall fall down and worship before him; shall bless and glorify him, and sing praises to the name of the Lord of spirits.
5Therefore the Elect and the Concealed One existed in his presence, before the world was created, and for ever.
6In his presence he existed, and has revealed to the saints and to the righteous the wisdom of the Lord of spirits; for
he has preserved the lot of the righteous, because they have hated and rejected this world of iniquity, and have detested all its works and ways, in the name of the Lord of spirits.

7For in his name shall they be preserved;61 and his will shall be their life. In those days shall the kings of the earth and the mighty men, who have gained the world by their achievements,62 become humble in countenance.
8For in the day of their anxiety and trouble their souls shall not be saved; and they shall bein subjection to63 those whom I have chosen.

9I will cast them like hay into the fire, and like lead into the water. Thus shall they burn in the presence of the righteous, and sink in the presence of the holy; nor shall a tenth part of them be found.
10But in the day of their trouble, the world shall obtain tranquillity.64

11In his presence shall they fall, and not be raised up again; nor shall there be any one to take them out of his hands, and to lift them up: for they have denied the Lord of spirits, and his Messiah. The name of the Lord of spirits shall be blessed.

notes: by the work of their own hands

b.p: <sup class="fn" data-fn="65">65</sup>
1Wisdom is poured forth like water, and glory fails not before him for ever and ever; for potent is he in all the secrets of righteousness.

2But iniquity passes away like a shadow, and possesses not a fixed station: for the Elect One stands before the Lord of spirits; and his glory is for ever and ever; and his power from generation to generation.
3With him dwells the spirit of intellectual wisdom, the spirit of instruction and of power, and the spirit of those who sleep in righteousness; he shall judge secret things.
4Nor shall any be able to utter a single word before him; for the Elect One is in the presence of the Lord of Spirits, according to his own pleasure.
1In those days the saints and the chosen shall undergo a change. The light of day shall rest upon them; and the splendor and glory of the saints shall be changed.
2In the day of trouble evil shall be heaped up upon sinners; but the righteous shall triumph in the name of the Lord of spirits.

3Others shall be made to see, that they must repent, and forsake the works of their hands; and that glory awaits them not in the presence of the Lord of spirits; yet that by his name they may be saved. The Lord of spirits will have compassion on them; for great is his mercy; and righteousness is in his judgment, and in the presence of his glory; nor in his judgment shall iniquity stand. He who repents not before him shall perish.
4Henceforward I will not have mercy on them, says the Lord of spirits.
1In those days shall the earth deliver up from her womb, and hell deliver up from hers, that which it has received; and destruction shall restore that which it owes.
2He shall select the righteous and holy from among them; for the day of their salvation has approached.
3And in those days shall the Elect One sit upon his throne, while every secret of intellectual wisdom shall proceed from his mouth, for the Lord of spirits has gifted and glorified him.
4In those days the mountains shall skip like rams, and the hills shall leap like young sheep66 satiated with milk; and all the righteous shall be like the angels in heaven.67
5Their countenance shall be bright with joy; for in those days shall the Elect One be exalted. The earth shall rejoice; the righteous shall inhabit it, and the elect possess it.68

notes: Jesus Christ appears to quote this "the righteous shall become like angels in heaven" and calls it "scripture," in Mark 12:25 and Matthew 22:30.

b.p: 1After that period, in the place where I had seen every secret sight, I was snatched up in a whirlwind, and carried off westwards.

2There my eyes beheld the secrets of heaven, and all which existed on earth; a mountain of iron, a mountain of copper,69 a mountain of silver, a mountain of gold, a mountain of fluid metal, and a mountain of lead.
3And I inquired of the angel who went with me, saying, What are these things, which in secret I behold?
4He said, All these things which you behold shall be for the dominion of the Messiah, that he may command, and be powerful upon earth.

5And that angel of peace answered me, saying, Wait but a short time, and you shalt understand, and every secret thing shall be revealed to you, which the Lord of spirits has decreed. Those mountains which you have seen, the mountain of iron, the mountain of copper, the mountain of silver, the mountain of gold, the mountain of fluid metal, and the mountain of lead, all these in the presence of the Elect One shall be like a honeycomb before the fire, and like water descending from above upon these mountains; and shall become debilitated before his feet.
6In those days men70 shall not be saved by gold and by silver.
7Nor shall they have it in their power to secure themselves, and to fly.
8There shall be neither iron for war, nor a coat of mail for the breast.
9Copper shall be useless; useless also that which neither rusts nor consumes away; and lead shall not be coveted.
10All these things shall be rejected, and perish from off the earth, when the Elect One shall appear in the presence of the Lord of spirits.
1There my eyes beheld a deep valley; and wide was its entrance.
2All who dwell on land, on the sea, and in islands, shall bring to it gifts, presents, and offerings; yet that deep valley

shall not be full. Their hands shall commit iniquity. Whatsoever they produce by labor, the sinners shall devour with crime. But they shall perish from the face of the Lord of spirits, and from the face of his earth. They shall stand up, and shall not fail for ever and ever.
3I beheld the angels of punishment, who were dwelling there, and preparing every instrument of Satan.
4Then I inquired of the angel of peace, who proceeded with me, for whom those instruments were preparing.
5He said, These they are preparing for the kings and71powerful ones of the earth, that thus they may perish.
6After which the righteous and chosen house of his congregation shall appear, and thenceforward unchangeable in the name of the Lord of spirits.
7Nor shall those mountains exist in his presence as the earth and the hills, as the fountains of water exist. And the righteous shall be relieved from the vexation of sinners.
1Then I looked and turned myself to another part of the earth, where I beheld a deep valley burning with fire.
2To this valley they brought monarchs and the mighty.
3And there my eyes beheld the instruments which they were making, fetters of iron without weight.72
4Then I inquired of the angel of peace, who proceeded with me, saying, For whom are these fetters and instruments prepared?
5He replied, These are prepared for the host of Azazeel, that they may be delivered over and adjudged to the lowest
condemnation; and that their angels may be overwhelmed with hurled stones, as the Lord of spirits has commanded.
